doc.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Writing, his own band and listening
title: Against microphones in live music
summary: He had microphones removed at the concert because live music should be written to sound right acoustically.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I think part of it was when I went up on stage after the North Texas Band breaking down I told them I don’t want to use all these microphones. Get rid of all these microphones. I can’t stand that sound.

I can’t stand that everybody’s got to have a mic, I can’t stand it. The music is written so that it will sound okay without the microphone. If you’ve got a flute solo and it’s overly orchestrated and you can’t hear the flute it’s your fault. I mean a recording session is different. But if you’re writing live music you’ve got to write live music that acoustically sounds right. And you learn that.
Right. And let the players balance.
